prompt: An e-commerce warehouse's error rate on orders tripled after it hired 40 seasonal workers. Which is the strongest initial hypothesis?

options.text: The warehouse software probably has a new bug.
options.feedback: Nothing points to the software. The errors tripled right after the new hires.

options.text: New staff, training, labels and layout are likely each to blame.
options.feedback: This lists causes without committing to one.

options.text: The new seasonal workers are likely making more of the picking errors.
options.feedback: Right. The timing points to the new hires. I'd compare error rates by worker tenure.

options.text: The new labels are probably confusing experienced staff.
options.feedback: This ignores the 40 new workers hired right before errors tripled.

explanation: The data shows order errors tripling after 40 seasonal workers joined. Likely cause: the new staff make more picking errors. To test it, compare error rates by worker tenure. If experienced staff's errors also rose, look at volume, labels or the software.
